headline: The logged data stops before the crossing you're apparently mid-way through. Nothing from the trail has landed here yet. Until it does, this reads as a clean post-taper baseline, not a race in progress.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The numbers on this card describe the state you carried into the start line, not what the trail has done to you since — no crossing sessions have arrived in the feed. On that pre-event picture, running volume eased slightly over the last four weeks against the prior block, which is exactly what a taper should look like and not a loss of anything. Strength stayed genuinely live into the final days, the last two sessions sitting lighter and shorter as you'd expect at the edge of a taper. Steps remain very high and essentially flat between training and rest days, so your background load never really dropped even as structured running did. The cardio-load status flashing "detraining" is a mechanical artefact of that taper — a low seven-day strain against a much larger 28-day base — not a real fitness signal, and it should invert sharply once trail days register. Recovery is the one genuinely mixed thread: the recent nights are erratic and several score as unrecorded, consistent with the travel-and-logistics window rather than settled trail rhythm.
sections.trends: The year-to-date comparison is the standout: you're carrying more than three times the distance to this date versus last year, which reframes the recent four-week dip entirely — it's a taper sitting on top of a very large base, not a plateau. The 16-week shape reads as a long build tapering to a deliberate point, which is coherent with heading into a major effort. This is the kind of accumulated volume that makes a multi-day crossing plausible rather than reckless.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchoring HR are unchanged across the 30-day window, so there's no drift in either direction to interpret — aerobic ceiling is stable. For a long-distance context that stability is the point: you're not chasing threshold gains right now, you're relying on a fixed, well-established engine to sit comfortably below it for hours. Nothing here suggests that engine has softened.
sections.zones: The pre-taper session shapes are appropriately polarised. The recent easy runs sit almost entirely in Z1–Z2 with low max HR, genuinely aerobic rather than grey-zone drift, while the one fast session before that carried real Z3–Z4 time — that's a clean hard/easy separation, not muddled middle-intensity. The long 18 km effort back in late July was the exception, a sustained Z3-heavy piece, but it stands alone rather than defining the block. For a taper into ultra distance, this distribution is right: sharpen once, then keep everything easy and low.
sections.hr_comparison: The strength sessions read as controlled circuit work — the most recent one nudged into Z2 briefly, the one before sat entirely in Z1, both well under any cardiovascular strain that would compete with running. Across the runs, the fallback-sourced sessions track closely with the chest-strap ones at matching efforts, so effort-level agreement is solid and I'd trust the easy-run HR figures as a like-for-like comparison. Nothing anomalous in either stream.
sections.calendar: The pre-taper rhythm shows tight run-cluster days — several short sessions stacked close together in early August rather than spread evenly — which is the classic taper pattern of frequent, short, low-cost touches to keep the system primed without accumulating fatigue. That's a deliberate shape, not fragmentation. The strength cadence stayed regular right up to the edge, which is what kept the lifting streak intact through the wind-down.
sections.personal_bests: None of the standing PBs are relevant to what you're doing right now — the short-course speed marks were set in a different phase and the crossing is a durability event, not a pace one. Your 50K/100-mile mark is the reference that matters here, and the real question is whether the current effort rewrites the ultra-distance line entirely; that won't show until the trail data lands.

watch_items: The obvious one: whether the crossing sessions actually appear in the feed — right now there's a gap between the narrative and the logged data, and the trail is the only evidence that counts.
Once trail data arrives, watch the cardio-load status flip out of its false "detraining" reading — the speed of that reversal will tell you how hard the first days loaded you.
Keep an eye on whether nightly recovery consolidates as trail rhythm replaces the logistics window, since the recent nights are still choppy.
